_meta.description: Single source of truth for the unified browser tool set. Every surface (matrx-extend Chrome extension, server-side Playwright, matrx-local desktop bridge) implements handlers that conform to these schemas. Tool definitions in public.tools are derived from this file via a one-shot migration; subsequent edits update both this file AND the DB through a single migration script. Do not add tools to public.tools by hand — the registry is this file.
consumers: DB migration script — seeds public.tools rows from this file
matrx-extend catalog generator — pnpm catalog:tools must produce names matching this file
Agent builder UI — pulls definitions for the user-facing tool picker

decisions.tabId_type: string — synthetic IDs are fine for Playwright surfaces; extension stringifies its int IDs at the boundary
decisions.tabs_list_scope: all tabs in the current window (Chrome's user-facing concept; tab-groups are out of scope for v1)
decisions.user_takeover: top-level tool (request_user_takeover), not a type on ask_user — different lifecycle
decisions.computer_zoom: removed from action enum — semantics were unclear, can re-add as screenshot_region if proven needed
decisions.computer_wait: removed from action enum — wait_for is the only blessed wait primitive
decisions.evaluate_javascript: admin-only by default, per-agent opt-in via tool_config — XSS-equivalent
decisions.browser_batch: no templating in v1 — model handles dependency between steps
decisions.memory_caps: 8 KB per value, 100 keys per session, documented in tool description
decisions.read_pdf: accepts tabId OR file_id (one required) — unified PDF reading path
decisions.drop_file: separate tool from upload_file — different DOM contract (DragEvent vs <input type=file>)

cloud_files_contract.principle: Every tool that produces or consumes file bytes uses cld_files via MediaRef. The agent never sees raw paths or base64.

producers.downloads.list rows: carry file_id and file_url; bytes already persisted at capture time
producers.get_request_body: returns inline body when small; returns {file_id, file_url, mime_type, size} when large

consumers.upload_file: takes file_ids: list[str] — handler resolves each MediaRef → bytes → temp file → element.set_input_files()
consumers.drop_file: takes file_id: str — handler resolves and synthesizes a DragEvent
consumers.read_pdf: accepts file_id as alternative to tabId

cloud_files_contract.implementation_notes: Each surface persists bytes via the same path: extension client POSTs to /files/upload (returning file_id); Playwright server calls persist_media_blobs_async in-process; matrx-local uploads via the same endpoint. The agent contract is identical across surfaces.

core.description: Recommended starter set for browser-capable agents. The agent-builder UI pre-checks these when creating a browser agent; clients (matrx-extend, etc.) typically pre-include them in the request's tools list. The server does NOT auto-inject — inclusion is always the agent definition's or the client's choice. The model can also reach the rest of the kit via load_browser_tools(category=...) at runtime if it wasn't pre-included.

inspection.description: Deep introspection and debugging tools. Include in the agent definition if the agent will inspect element internals, console output, or network traffic; otherwise reachable via load_browser_tools(category='inspection') at runtime.

files.description: File handling — uploads, downloads, PDF reading. Include when the agent will work with files. All bytes flow through cld_files / MediaRef.

interaction.description: Escalation and clipboard primitives. Include when the agent may need to hand control to the user (auth, sensitive input) or use the system clipboard.

advanced.description: Power-user and admin-gated tools. evaluate_javascript is admin-only by default. Include in the agent definition only if the standard kit is insufficient for the agent's purpose.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Get an accessibility-tree representation of the page with stable element reference IDs (e.g. ref_1) usable by other tools. Returns all elements by default. Refs invalidate on navigation. If output exceeds max_chars, narrow with ref_id or reduce depth. Set trigger_lazy_load=true on SPAs that defer rendering (Notion, Linear, modern Gmail) — the handler scrolls to bottom + waits for network idle + scrolls back before snapshotting.

ref_id.description: Focus on this element and its descendants only.

trigger_lazy_load.description: Force lazy-loaded content to render before snapshotting. Adds 1–3 seconds.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Locate elements by natural-language description (e.g. 'search bar', 'add to cart button'). Returns up to 20 matches with reference IDs. Use a more specific query if too many results. For literal text matching, use find_text_on_page instead.

query.description: Natural-language description of the target element.

tools.name: get_page_text
tools.description: Extract readable text content from a page, prioritizing article body (Mozilla Readability). Use for long-form reading instead of read_page when full DOM is unnecessary.

tools.name: find_text_on_page
tools.description: Literal Ctrl+F-style text search within a tab. Returns matches with surrounding context and refs to the containing elements. Use this instead of get_page_text when you only need to know if/where specific text appears. For natural-language search, use find instead.

regex.description: Treat query as a regex. Default false.

tools.name: computer
tools.description: Mouse, keyboard, and screenshot interactions. Prefer 'ref' over 'coordinate' when targeting elements; coordinates survive poorly across scrolls and layout changes. The 'screenshot' action persists the image to cloud and returns {file_id, file_url, width, height, mime_type} — use that file_id with upload_file or drop_file later. Use wait_for for synchronization, NOT a fixed sleep.

coordinate.description: [x, y] in viewport pixels. Required for click/hover/drag end position when no 'ref'.

ref.description: Element reference from read_page/find. Alternative to coordinate for click/hover. Required for scroll_to.

text.description: Required for 'type' (text to type) and 'key' (e.g. 'Enter', 'cmd+a', space-separated for sequences).

output_schema_notes.screenshot: { file_id: string, file_url: string, width: number, height: number, mime_type: string }

tools.name: form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element by reference. Use string for text inputs, boolean for checkboxes/radios, value or visible label for selects. The handler dispatches on element type — you don't need to specify it.

value.description: Value to set. Type depends on input kind.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate a tab to a URL, or move through history with 'back'/'forward'. Protocol defaults to https:// if omitted. After navigating, refs from prior read_page calls are invalidated — call read_page again before referencing elements.

force.description: If true, discard unsaved changes when a 'Leave site?' dialog appears.

tools.name: tabs
tools.description: Manage browser tabs. Actions: 'list' (returns all tabs in the current window with IDs/titles/URLs — call when you don't have a tabId), 'create' (opens a new tab and returns its ID; pass url to open it directly at a URL), 'close' (closes a tab by ID), 'switch' (brings a tab to the foreground so the user sees it), 'reload' (refreshes a tab). tabId is required for close/switch/reload.

tabId.description: Target tab. Required for close, switch, reload.

url.description: Optional URL for 'create' — opens the new tab at this URL in a single round trip.

tools.name: wait_for
tools.description: Poll until a condition is met or timeout. Use after navigation or actions that trigger async loads — far more reliable than fixed sleeps. Conditions: 'element' (ref or selector exists and is visible; pass scroll=true to scroll the page while polling — handles infinite scroll), 'text' (text appears anywhere on page), 'url' (tab URL matches substring or regex), 'network_idle' (no in-flight requests for ~500ms).

target.description: Element ref/selector, text string, or URL pattern. Required for element/text/url.

scroll.description: For condition='element' only — scroll the page while polling so virtualized/infinite-scroll content can render the target into view.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Pause and ask the user a question when input is needed to proceed (ambiguity, missing info, required confirmation). Use 'confirm' for yes/no, 'choice' for a fixed set of options, 'text' for free-form input, 'secret' for sensitive input (passwords, API keys, MFA codes — masked in UI and storage, response value tagged sensitive). Prefer this over guessing on destructive or sensitive actions. For full control transfer (user types into the actual page), use request_user_takeover.

question.description: The question to show the user.

context.description: Optional one-line context for why you're asking.

tools.name: notify_user
tools.description: Send a one-way status update to the user without pausing for a response. Use sparingly for milestones in long tasks. Do NOT use to ask questions — use ask_user for that.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Write or revise the plan for the current task and surface it to the user before executing. Use at the start of any non-trivial multi-step task, and again whenever the plan materially changes. Listed domains become approved for the session when the user accepts.

domains.description: Domains the plan will visit, e.g. ['github.com', 'stackoverflow.com'].

tools.name: get_element_details
tools.description: Deep inspection of a single element by ref: full attribute set, computed styles, bounding box, visibility, and innerHTML. Use when read_page's summary isn't enough — e.g. reading data-* attributes or checking if something is hidden by CSS. Avoids needing evaluate_javascript for routine introspection. innerHTML is capped at 50 KB; response includes truncated:true when exceeded.

tools.name: read_console_messages
tools.description: Read browser console messages (log/warn/error) from a tab. Always pass a 'pattern' to filter — unfiltered output is usually overwhelming. Set clear=true after reading to avoid duplicate reporting on the next call.

clear.description: Clear after reading to avoid duplicates next call.

tools.name: read_network_requests
tools.description: Read HTTP requests (XHR, fetch, documents, etc.) from a tab. Auto-cleared on cross-domain navigation. Filter with urlPattern to keep output manageable. Response bodies are NOT included by default — use get_request_body to fetch a specific body. The buffer is per-tab and bounded; old entries fall off the back.

include_body.description: Include response bodies inline. Off by default — bodies are huge. Use get_request_body for a specific request instead.

tools.name: get_request_body
tools.description: Fetch the response body for a specific request seen by read_network_requests. Returns inline text when small (<256 KB); returns {file_id, file_url, mime_type, size} when larger so the body lives in cloud and the agent can reference it without burning context.

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Upload one or more files to a <input type='file'> element by reference. Pass file_ids — these are MediaRef IDs (e.g. from a previous /files/upload, or from computer.action=screenshot, or from any prior tool that returned a file_id). The handler resolves each file_id to bytes and calls element.set_input_files(). Do NOT click file inputs — that opens a native picker the agent cannot see. For drag-and-drop targets, use drop_file instead.

ref.description: Reference of the file input element.

file_ids.description: List of MediaRef file_ids. Resolved server-side regardless of which surface is executing.

tools.name: drop_file
tools.description: Synthesize a drag-and-drop of a single file onto a target element or coordinate. Use for drop zones that aren't backed by <input type='file'>. Provide ref OR coordinate, not both. file_id is a MediaRef (e.g. from a prior screenshot or upload) — bytes are resolved server-side.

file_id.description: MediaRef of the file to drop.

coordinate.description: [x, y] drop target for visible drop zones when ref isn't available.

filename.description: Override filename in the synthesized DragEvent. Defaults to the cld_files filename.

tools.name: downloads
tools.description: Manage file downloads triggered by the page or agent. Bytes are auto-persisted to cld_files at capture time; rows in 'list' carry file_id and file_url so you can reference downloaded content immediately. Actions: 'list' (returns pending/completed downloads with downloadId, file_id, file_url, filename, size, source, status), 'confirm' (user-permission step that exposes the file in the user-facing UI), 'cancel' (aborts and deletes the cloud row). Surface downloads via ask_user before 'confirm'.

tools.name: read_pdf
tools.description: Extract text and structure from a PDF — either one loaded in a browser tab, or one already in cld_files (pass file_id). Returns text by page with optional page range. Use file_id when you have a MediaRef in hand (e.g. from a prior download); use tabId when the PDF is open in the browser.

tabId.description: Tab displaying the PDF (one of tabId or file_id required).

file_id.description: MediaRef of a PDF in cld_files (one of tabId or file_id required).

tools.name: request_user_takeover
tools.description: Hand keyboard/mouse control to the user so they can perform an action the agent cannot or should not (logging in, MFA, CAPTCHA, sensitive form filling, decisions only the user can make). The user types/clicks directly into the page; when they're done they signal completion in the UI. The tool resolves with no model-visible value — the agent should re-read the page after takeover ends to see what changed. Distinct from ask_user, which is Q&A.

tabId.description: Tab where the user should act.

reason.description: One-line explanation surfaced to the user (e.g. 'Please log in — I cannot handle your password').

expected_action.description: Optional concrete description of what the user should do (e.g. 'Enter your password and click Login').

tools.name: clipboard
tools.description: Read from or write to the system clipboard. Actions: 'read' (returns current clipboard text), 'write' (sets clipboard text). Useful for 'copy this for the user' and 'paste what I just copied' workflows. Requires the clipboard Chrome permission on the extension surface.

tools.name: evaluate_javascript
tools.description: Evaluate JavaScript in the page context. Returns the value of the last expression — do NOT use 'return' at top level. Admin-gated by default; non-admin agents must be explicitly granted via tool_config. Prefer DOM tools (read_page, find, computer, form_input) when possible — JS exec is XSS-equivalent and bypasses our safety nets.

text.description: JavaScript source. Last expression is returned.

tools.name: resize_window
tools.description: Resize the browser viewport for the tab's window. Useful for responsive testing. Note: this is viewport size, not OS-window size.

tools.name: browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of tool calls in one round trip. Runs sequentially, stops on first error. Use for predictable multi-step flows (click → type → key) where each step doesn't depend on the prior result. If a step needs a value from a prior step (e.g. find then click(ref)), use separate calls — batch does NOT support templating in v1. Cannot be nested. Returns {succeeded: [...], failed_at: int|null, error: ...}.

input.description: Exact input object for that tool.

tools.name: memory
tools.description: Session-scoped scratchpad for stashing structured notes across turns without burning context tokens. Actions: 'set' (write a value to a key), 'get' (read by key), 'list' (all keys), 'delete' (remove a key). Values are stringified — stringify objects before passing. Caps: 8 KB per value, 100 keys per session. Cleared at session end.

value.description: Required for set. Max 8 KB. Stringify objects before passing.

tools.name: record_gif
tools.description: Record browser actions and export as an animated GIF. Actions: 'start_recording', 'stop_recording', 'export' (generates and either downloads or drops onto a page element), 'clear' (discard frames). Take a screenshot right after start and right before stop to capture clean first/last frames. 'export' returns {file_id, file_url} when not dropping. Drop target accepts ref (preferred) or coordinate.

tabId.description: Tab whose group this applies to.

download.description: Download instead of drag-drop. For 'export' only.

ref.description: Drop target element reference. For 'export' when not downloading.

coordinate.description: [x, y] drop target. Fallback when ref isn't available.

options.description: Optional GIF rendering toggles. For 'export' only.
